purpose: Install pinned Context Mode, ai-memory and MCPorter from recipes/README.md (adoption/manifest.json recipe_map) into brand-new prefixes with no shared cache, then run each tool's version check plus one functional call, narrowing open_gaps[recovery-portability][1] (only uv's clean-prefix install had been executed; Context Mode, ai-memory and MCPorter had not).
preregistered: If all three tools install into fresh, previously-nonexistent prefixes and each passes a version/identity check plus one real functional call (Context Mode: doctor + index + search a scratch note under an isolated CONTEXT_MODE_DIR; ai-memory: init + write-page + search against a disposable data dir AND a disposable server bound via AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL on a non-default port, never the live 127.0.0.1:49374 instance; MCPorter: list + a real tool call against that disposable ai-memory MCP endpoint), that settles open_gaps[1]'s 'needs clean-install qualification for Context Mode, ai-memory and MCPorter' item as executed. Any non-zero exit, any command that silently reaches the live ai-memory server instead of the named disposable one, or an empty/error functional result would refute this and must be recorded, not smoothed over.

result: All three tools installed cleanly into brand-new prefixes (none pre-existed) and each passed a version/identity check plus a real functional call. Context Mode 1.0.169 at the pinned commit ran doctor (storage PASS), indexed a scratch note and returned it verbatim from search, all under an isolated CONTEXT_MODE_DIR. ai-memory 2.3.2 initialised a disposable data dir, started a disposable HTTP server on a non-default port (127.0.0.1:49475, distinct from the live 127.0.0.1:49374 instance which stayed up and untouched throughout, confirmed by `ss -ltnp` showing the live server's own pid before and after), and a write-page/search round trip through that disposable server via AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL succeeded. MCPorter 0.13.13 connected to that same disposable ai-memory MCP endpoint, listed its tool catalog, and executed a real memory_query tool call that returned the just-written page. This narrows open_gaps[1] from 'not executed' to 'clean-install and one functional call executed for all three named components'.

verdict_impact.explanation: Confirms all three selected components (Context Mode, ai-memory, MCPorter) install and function correctly from a completely fresh prefix with no shared cache or pre-existing state, supporting their continued incumbent status. Does not by itself establish a second physical host (open_gaps[7,9] remain open) and does not repeat the uv clean-prefix evidence (already established).

limitations: Single-run per tool, no retry per the preregistration rule.
This remains one prefix on the same existing WSL host, not a second physical or virtual machine; open_gaps[7] and [9] (an actually adopted new physical host) are unaffected.

An earlier status command in this same session was run with AI_MEMORY_DATA_DIR set but AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL unset before this check's disposable server was started; `status --json` in that state read the live server at the default port (a read-only query: version/counts only, no write, and no data was altered). All subsequent commands in this receipt explicitly set AI_MEMORY_SERVER_URL to the disposable 127.0.0.1:49475 endpoint as required. Recorded here rather than omitted.

Context Mode's functional call exercised its FTS5 index/search path only, not full MCP stdio server registration with an actual Claude/Codex client, since that would edit the shared user plugin marketplace/settings that other concurrent sessions' Context Mode processes depend on -- explicitly off-limits for this unit. Native plugin marketplace registration for Context Mode remains unexercised by this receipt.
MCPorter's npm install tarball integrity relied on npm's own registry integrity check (dist.integrity), not an independent sha256 recorded here.

ai-memory's disposable server briefly logged that it would fetch its default local embedding model in the background (~87MB); no embedding-provider override was set, so this is a text/FTS functional check that also began a first-run model download, consistent with the recipe's documented default behaviour, not a deliberate embedding_provider=none trial.
